chains.title: NKRF-binding loss may derepress TERT

links.claim: NKRF is the leading non-null candidate but occupancy in the disease context is unresolved: NKRF has its own QBiC-SELEX model and the ref G allele binds more strongly than alt A (effect -0.514, z -12.31), with the ref allele at the 99.0th percentile, a strong site. ENCODE ChIP-seq has an NKRF peak over the variant only in GM12878, not glioblastoma; E36 reports no glioblastoma-matching NKRF peak, and E04 states no ENCODE biosample matches the expression context. NKRF is chosen over other ChIP-positive expressed TFs because it has the clearest strong-site allelic effect in this set, but this is not evidence of NKRF occupancy in glioblastoma.
The variant lies within the Ensembl enhancer ENSR5_C5GP and within 75 bp of TERT-associated pELS/PLS cCREs; no cCRE directly overlaps the variant, so the element assignment is annotation-level.
TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene at 0.5 kb upstream and has the best L2G score, 0.84; the L2G comes from a hypertension credible set with PIP 0.00, not a cancer GWAS or molecular QTL.

NKRF is expressed in DepMap glioblastoma lines, but only at 8.69 TPM, rank 522 of 1626 TFs; glioblastoma is the provided expression context, and TERT is broadly relevant in glioblastoma, melanoma, and bladder cancer literature.

The phenotype link is conditional and unproven: if NKRF represses TERT, weaker NKRF binding on alt A would derepress TERT and increase telomerase activity. E35 did not identify direct NKRF-TERT repression evidence, so this direction remains an assumption.

predictions: NKRF occupies this element in glioblastoma cells and ref G binds NKRF more than alt A.
If NKRF represses TERT, alt A increases TERT expression and NKRF depletion mimics the alt allele.
The alt-associated TERT increase is reduced or abolished when NKRF is overexpressed.
falsified_if: Allele-specific NKRF ChIP shows no NKRF occupancy or no ref-greater binding at this base in glioblastoma cells.
NKRF depletion does not change TERT expression in glioblastoma cells.
NKRF acts as an activator rather than a repressor of TERT.

chains.title: CREB1-binding gain may activate TERT

links.claim: CREB1 is a secondary candidate: its QBiC-SELEX model is CIS-BP-mapped from CREM, so it reflects CREB/CREM family specificity rather than a CREB1-only model. It shows alt A binds more strongly than ref G (effect 0.244, z 6.24), with the alt allele at the 98.7th percentile, a strong site. ENCODE ChIP-seq has a CREB1 peak over the variant only in H1, not glioblastoma; occupancy in the disease context is not established.
The variant lies within ENSR5_C5GP and near TERT-associated pELS/PLS cCREs, consistent with a TERT regulatory element, though no cCRE directly overlaps the variant.
TERT is the nearest gene at 0.5 kb upstream and the best L2G gene at this locus, with the same hypertension/PIP 0.00 caveat.
CREB1 is expressed in DepMap glioblastoma lines at 30.94 TPM, rank 132 of 1626 TFs; TERT relevance in glioblastoma, melanoma, and bladder cancer is supported only by broad literature.

The phenotype link is conditional and unproven: if CREB1 activates TERT, stronger CREB1 binding on alt A would increase TERT expression. E37 did not provide specific CREB1-TERT activation evidence, so this direction remains an assumption.

predictions: CREB1 occupies this element in a permissive cell type and alt A increases CREB1 occupancy.
If CREB1 activates TERT, alt A increases TERT expression and CREB1 knockdown reduces the alt-associated increase.
The effect requires the CREB/CREM family site at this base.
falsified_if: CREB1 does not occupy this element in glioblastoma cells.
Allele-specific CREB1 ChIP shows no alt-greater binding at this base.
CREB1 perturbation does not affect TERT expression in the relevant cells.

chains.title: JUN weak-site gain may activate TERT

links.claim: JUN has its own QBiC-SELEX model showing alt A binds more strongly than ref G (effect 0.111, z 5.95), but the site is weak on both alleles, with the better allele at only the 85.4th percentile. ENCODE ChIP-seq has a JUN peak over the variant only in A549, not glioblastoma; JUN is highly expressed in glioblastoma, but the weak site makes it unlikely that JUN acts through this exact base.
The variant lies within ENSR5_C5GP and near TERT-associated pELS/PLS cCREs, consistent with a TERT regulatory element, though direct regulatory function in glioblastoma is not shown.
TERT is the nearest gene and best L2G gene at this locus, with the hypertension/PIP 0.00 caveat.
JUN is strongly expressed in DepMap glioblastoma lines at 91.65 TPM, rank 16 of 1626 TFs; TERT disease relevance rests on broad literature only.

The phenotype link is conditional and unproven: if JUN activates TERT through this element, the small alt-gain in JUN binding would weakly increase TERT expression. No cited evidence establishes JUN-TERT regulation at this element.

predictions: JUN occupancy at this element is weak and alt A produces at most a small increase.
JUN perturbation changes TERT expression only if this element is active in the tested cell type.
The effect is smaller than for a strong-site TF such as NKRF.
falsified_if: JUN does not occupy this element in glioblastoma cells.
The site is too weak for JUN to act through this base in vivo.
JUN perturbation does not change TERT expression.

grades_v0.reason: No non-null chain has a TF occupancy peak at this variant in glioblastoma or the provided expression context. E04 explicitly says no ENCODE biosample matches the expression context, so all ChIP support is from other biosamples. All phenotype links are missing because E18 is only generic TERT-cancer literature and does not establish TF-TERT direction. The TERT gene link is supported by proximity/L2G, but the L2G comes from a hypertension credible set with PIP 0.00 and no cancer GWAS/eQTL. The element link is supported for location in an Ensembl enhancer near TERT-associated cCREs, but no cCRE overlaps the variant and no glioblastoma enhancer assay is cited. NKRF is overcalled 'best-supported': it has the strongest QBiC-SELEX effect and a strong site, but only GM12878 occupancy and low glioblastoma expression rank.

E01 directly annotates ENSR5_C5GP as an enhancer and places the variant in it; E03 shows the nearest pELS/PLS cCREs are 75 bp/500 bp away and list TERT as nearby. The exact location claim is supported, although 'TERT regulatory region' remains an annotation-level inference.
E02 puts TERT 0.5 kb from the TSS and E16 gives TERT the best L2G score, 0.84. The claim is directly supported, but the genetic context is hypertension with PIP 0.00, not cancer.

E20 supports NKRF expression in DepMap glioblastoma lines, but at 8.69 TPM and rank 522 of 1626 TFs. E18 gives only literature-title support that TERT is relevant in these cancers, with no bladder-specific and no NKRF-specific evidence.

E18 does not show that NKRF represses TERT or that NKRF acts at this element. The chain explicitly admits NKRF repression is inferred, so the mechanistic phenotype link is missing. The direction is internally consistent only if NKRF is a repressor: ref binds more, alt binds less, so alt would derepress TERT.

E21 shows an alt-gain QBiC-SELEX effect (z 6.24) with a strong alt site, but the best model is CIS-BP-mapped from CREM, and occupancy is only in H1 (E09). No glioblastoma occupancy is established, so this is weak rather than supported.
Same element evidence as above: E01 places the variant in ENSR5_C5GP and E03 shows nearby TERT-associated cCREs. The location claim is supported; direct TERT-enhancer function is not proven.
E02 gives TERT as nearest gene at 0.5 kb, and E16 gives TERT L2G 0.84. Supported as stated, with the same hypertension/PIP caveat.
E21 supports CREB1 expression in DepMap glioblastoma (30.94 TPM, rank 132). E18 is only broad TERT-cancer literature and does not establish CREB1 function in these cancers.

No cited evidence shows CREB1 activates TERT. E18 is about TERT in cancer generally, not CREB1-TERT regulation. Direction is consistent only if CREB1 is an activator: alt binds more, so alt would increase TERT.

E27 shows an alt-gain QBiC-SELEX effect (z 5.95), but the site is weak on both alleles (best allele 85.4th percentile, below the 97.5th strong-site threshold), and occupancy is only in A549 (E05). No glioblastoma occupancy; weak.
E01/E03 support enhancer/cCRE proximity to TERT as above; direct regulatory function in glioblastoma is not shown.
E02 and E16 support TERT as nearest and best L2G gene, with the same non-cancer GWAS caveat.
JUN expression is strongly supported in DepMap glioblastoma (91.65 TPM, rank 16; E27), but TERT disease relevance again rests on broad E18 literature only.
No cited evidence shows JUN activates TERT through this element. E18 does not address JUN-TERT regulation. Direction is consistent only if JUN is an activator.

E34 gives a very large alt-gain QBiC-SELEX effect (z 67.98), but the best model is a HOXD4 homeodomain model shared across multiple related factors, and occupancy is unknown because ENCODE never assayed HOXB2. The TF identity is therefore not resolved; at best weak.
E01/E03 support enhancer/cCRE proximity as above; no direct HOXB2 or homeodomain occupancy at the element is shown.
E02 and E16 support TERT as nearest and best L2G gene, with the same hypertension/PIP caveat.
E34 supports HOXB2 expression in DepMap glioblastoma at 10.25 TPM, rank 454, which is low relative to other TFs. E18 is broad TERT-cancer literature only.

No cited evidence establishes that HOXB2 or any homeodomain factor activates TERT. E18 does not address this. The chain also lacks a reason to choose HOXB2 specifically over EN1, HOXA1, HOXA2, HOXA4 or other factors sharing the same mapped model.

grades_final.reason: QBiC-SELEX shows ref G binds NKRF more strongly with a strong site (E20), but NKRF ChIP occupancy over the variant is reported only in GM12878; E36 and E04 state no glioblastoma/matched biosample occupancy. Occupancy in the disease context is missing, so this is one-of-two and weak.

E01 directly places the variant in ENSR5_C5GP enhancer, and E03 directly states no cCRE overlaps but the nearest pELS is 75 bp away with TERT-associated cCREs nearby. This supports the annotation-level element claim, not a functional glioblastoma element.

E02 shows TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene at 0.5 kb, and E16 gives TERT as best L2G at 0.84, but that L2G is from a hypertension credible set with PIP 0.00 and there is no molecular QTL. The target-gene link is therefore indirect.

E20 directly shows NKRF expression in DepMap glioblastoma lines, but at low level (8.69 TPM, rank 522/1626). E18 is broad TERT-cancer literature, not matched glioblastoma variant or NKRF-TERT evidence, so cell-type relevance is only weakly supported.
E35 did not identify direct NKRF-TERT repression evidence; E18 is broad TERT-disease literature. The claimed derepression direction is explicitly conditional and unproven.

QBiC-SELEX shows alt A binds more strongly (E21), but the model is CIS-BP-mapped from CREM and CREB1 ChIP occupancy over the variant is only in H1, not glioblastoma; E04 confirms no matched biosample. Occupancy in the disease context is missing, so weak.

E01 directly places the variant in ENSR5_C5GP enhancer, and E03 directly supports nearby TERT-associated pELS/PLS cCREs while noting no direct cCRE overlap. The annotation-level element claim is supported.
E02 supports TERT as nearest gene and E16 gives TERT as best L2G, but the credible set is hypertension with PIP 0.00 and no molecular QTL. The gene link is indirect.

E21 directly shows CREB1 expression in DepMap glioblastoma lines (30.94 TPM, rank 132/1626), but there is no matched glioblastoma occupancy or variant-specific TERT evidence; E18 is broad literature. Cell-type support is weak.
E37 did not provide specific CREB1-TERT activation evidence, and E18 is broad TERT-disease literature. The activation direction remains an assumption.
QBiC-SELEX shows a small alt-greater JUN effect (E27), but the site is weak on both alleles and JUN ChIP occupancy over the variant is only in A549, not glioblastoma. The binding link is weak.
E01 directly places the variant in ENSR5_C5GP enhancer, and E03 supports nearby TERT-associated cCREs with no direct overlap. The element assignment is supported at annotation level.
E02 supports TERT as nearest gene and E16 gives TERT as best L2G, but the credible set has PIP 0.00 and is for hypertension, with no molecular QTL. The gene link is weak.

E27 directly shows high JUN expression in DepMap glioblastoma lines (91.65 TPM, rank 16/1626), but there is no matched glioblastoma occupancy and TERT disease relevance rests on broad literature only. Cell-type support is weak overall.
No cited evidence establishes JUN-TERT regulation at this element; E18 is broad TERT-disease literature only. The phenotype direction is conditional and unproven.

Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap subtype median Glioblastoma), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 10 occupied (4 with a strong site), 5 of 109 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 0 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 563 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
